title: The image of a regular homomorphism is closed
statement:
Let $G\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(V)$ and $K\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(W)$
be closed reduced matrix groups over $k=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and
let $\varphi:G\to K$ be a regular homomorphism, that is, a morphism of
varieties which is a group homomorphism on $k$-points. Then the image
$S=\varphi(G(k))$ is a closed subgroup of $K(k)$: it is the set of
$k$-points of a closed subgroup of $K$, which we equip with its reduced
structure.

proof.text:
Since $\varphi$ is a homomorphism, $S$ is a subgroup of $K(k)$. For any
subgroup $H\subseteq K(k)$ its Zariski closure $\overline H$ is again a
subgroup: for fixed $y\in H$ the closed condition $xy\in\overline H$
holds on $H$, hence on $\overline H$; then for fixed $x\in\overline H$
the closed condition $xy\in\overline H$ holds on $H$, hence on
$\overline H$; inversion is the same argument.

First treat the identity component. By
[lem-wf-algebraic-component-cosets], $G^\circ$ is an irreducible closed
subset of the affine variety $\operatorname{GL}(V)$, hence an
irreducible affine variety. Put $S_0=\varphi(G^\circ(k))$, a subgroup of
$S$, and let $T=\overline{S_0}\subseteq K$ with its reduced structure.
Then $T$ is a closed subgroup; it is irreducible as the closure of the
image of an irreducible space, and it is affine, being closed in
$\operatorname{GL}(W)$. The morphism $\varphi|_{G^\circ}:G^\circ\to T$ is a
morphism of affine schemes of finite type over $k$, so by part (1) of
[lem-wf-affine-constructible-open] its image
$\varphi(G^\circ)\subseteq T$ is constructible. It is dense in $T$,
because its closed points $S_0$ are already dense; hence part (2)
of [lem-wf-affine-constructible-open] gives a nonempty open
$U\subseteq T$ contained in the image. On $k$-points: every closed
point $t\in U$ has a nonempty fibre, which is a nonempty finite-type
$k$-scheme and therefore has a $k$-point because $k$ is algebraically
closed; hence $U(k)\subseteq S_0$, and $U(k)\neq\varnothing$.

Now

$$
U(k)^{-1}U(k)=\bigcup_{u\in U(k)}u^{-1}U(k)
$$

is the set of $k$-points of an open neighbourhood of the identity in
$T$, and it lies in the subgroup $S_0$. Its translates $sU^{-1}U$ for
$s\in S_0$ show that $S_0$ is open in $T(k)$; the other cosets of $S_0$
in $T(k)$ are open for the same reason, so $S_0$ is also closed in
$T(k)$. Since $S_0$ is dense in $T$, we get $S_0=T(k)$. Thus
$\varphi(G^\circ(k))$ is the set of $k$-points of the closed subgroup
$T$.

Finally, by [lem-wf-algebraic-component-cosets] the group $G(k)$ is the
union of finitely many cosets $g_1G^\circ(k),\ldots,g_nG^\circ(k)$ (as
in [def-wf-algebraic-components], $G^\circ$ is the identity component).
Therefore

$$
S=\bigcup_{i=1}^n\varphi(g_i)\,T(k),
$$

a finite union of translates of the closed set $T(k)$. Each translate
is closed, so $S$ is the set of $k$-points of the closed reduced
subvariety $\bigcup_i\varphi(g_i)T$ of $K$, which is a subgroup because
$S$ is and closed subvarieties of $K$ are determined by their
$k$-points.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:G\to K$ be a homomorphism of group schemes over an algebraically
closed field $L$, where $G$ is of finite type and $K$ is locally of
finite type over $L$. Then the image $f(G)$ is a closed subset of $K$.

*Complement.* Let $G\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(V)$ and
$K\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(W)$ be closed reduced matrix groups over
$L$, and let $\varphi:G\to K$ be a regular homomorphism, that is, a
morphism of varieties which is a group homomorphism on $L$-points. Then
$S=\varphi(G(L))$ is a closed subgroup of $K(L)$: it is the set of
$L$-points of a closed subgroup of $K$, which we equip with its reduced
structure.

proof.text:
Put $S=f(G(L))$; since $f$ is a homomorphism, $S$ is a subgroup of
$K(L)$. Let $W\subseteq K$ be an affine open. Since $G$ is of finite
type, $f^{-1}(W)$ is covered by finitely many affine opens of finite type
over $L$, so Chevalley's theorem, part (1) of
[lem-wf-affine-constructible-open], shows that $f(G)\cap W$ is
constructible in $W$; thus $f(G)$ is locally constructible in $K$.
The closed points of $K$ are its $L$-points, and a closed point
$t\in f(G)$ has a nonempty fibre, which is a scheme of finite type over
$L$ and therefore has an $L$-point
([lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing]). Hence the $L$-points of
$f(G)$ are exactly $S$.

Let $J$ be the closure of $f(G)$ in $K$, with its reduced structure.
Closed points are dense in every locally constructible subset of a scheme
locally of finite type over $L$, so $J$ is the closure of $S$ and $J(L)$
is the closure of $S$ in $K(L)$. The closure of a
subgroup $H\subseteq K(L)$ is again a subgroup: for fixed $y\in H$ the
closed condition $xy\in\overline H$ holds on $H$, hence on $\overline H$;
then for fixed $x\in\overline H$ the closed condition $xy\in\overline H$
holds on $H$, hence on $\overline H$; inversion is the same argument.
Since $J\times_LJ$ is reduced and its closed points are the pairs of
$L$-points ([lem-wf-affine-product-reduced], applied to products of
affine opens of $J$), the vanishing principle of
[lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] shows that multiplication and
inversion of $K$ restrict to $J$. Thus $J$ is a closed subgroup scheme
of $K$.

The locally constructible set $f(G)$ is dense in $J$, so by part (2) of
[lem-wf-affine-constructible-open], applied in an affine open of $J$
meeting $f(G)$, it contains a nonempty open $U\subseteq J$; then $U(L)\subseteq S$ and $U(L)\neq\varnothing$. Pick
$u\in U(L)$. Translations of $J$ by its $L$-points are automorphisms of
$J$ ([lem-sc-translation-automorphism]), so $u^{-1}U$ is an open
neighbourhood of $1$ in $J$ with $L$-points in $S$, and the translates
$s\,u^{-1}U$ with $s\in S$ show that $S$ is open in $J(L)$. The other
cosets of $S$ in $J(L)$ are open for the same reason, so $S$ is also
closed in $J(L)$. Since $S$ is dense in $J(L)$, we get $S=J(L)$.

Finally, $J\smallsetminus f(G)$ is locally constructible and contains no
closed point. A nonempty constructible subset of an affine scheme of
finite type over $L$ contains a nonempty locally closed subset, hence a
closed point; applying this in the affine opens of $J$ shows that
$J\smallsetminus f(G)$ is empty, so $f(G)=J$ is closed. In summary, the
closure $J$ of $f(G)$, with its reduced structure, is a closed subgroup
scheme of $K$ with $f(G)=J$ and $J(L)=f(G(L))$.

For the complement, a closed reduced matrix group is a group scheme of
finite type over $L$, and a regular homomorphism between reduced matrix
groups is a homomorphism of group schemes, because the identities
expressing it are identities of regular maps on reduced varieties that
hold on $L$-points ([lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing],
[lem-wf-affine-product-reduced]). Applying the argument above to
$f=\varphi$, the set $S=\varphi(G(L))$ is the set of $L$-points of the
closure $J$ of $\varphi(G)$, which with its reduced structure is a
closed subgroup of $K$. In particular $S$ is a closed subgroup of
$K(L)$.
